critical_code_review_comments: [VERIFIED CLEAN] server.py line 906: `total_revenue`: round(sum(inv["total"] for inv in invs), 2) — generator variable `inv` is bound by the `for inv in invs` clause (no shadowing of outer `i` left over). Tests confirm correct sums and matching by_payment_mode breakdown.
[VERIFIED CLEAN] server.py line ~939-950: PublicBookingIn._when uses `dt = datetime.fromisoformat(...)` and returns `dt.isoformat()`. Past/invalid/business-hours all rejected with 422.

[VERIFIED CLEAN] POS.jsx printInvoice: escapeHtml applied to invoice_no, customer_name, staff_name, payment_mode, item.name, and date. Iframe approach (position:fixed;w:0;h:0;visibility:hidden;srcdoc) — no popup, removed after 1s via setTimeout. Note: srcdoc inherits parent's CSP and isolates the print context — XSS payload cannot escape into the parent page. Good fix.

[VERIFIED CLEAN] BookPublic.jsx:179 — featured review keyed by `r.id || \`featured-${idx}\`` (id-first with array-index fallback for backward safety). 3 featured reviews rendered with zero React duplicate-key warnings.

[MINOR/LATENT] POS.jsx printInvoice: the inline iframe.onload handler swallows printing errors silently and still removes the iframe after 1s. If contentWindow.print() throws (e.g., headless context), user sees 'Unable to open print dialog' toast — good. But the 1s removal timer may fire before slow browsers complete print queueing on very large invoices; consider hooking afterprint event or using a longer timer for invoices with >50 items.

[MINOR/CARRIED] Pre-existing pytest_results.xml warns about /api/public/book and /api/public/referral/{code} (non-slug variants) returning 404 — already documented in iter5 action items; backend has slug-required routes only. Iter6 did not change this; user-facing app uses /api/public/book/{slug} correctly.

The iter5 iframe-creation instrumentation in playwright (override of document.body.appendChild to capture iframe.srcdoc) is a reliable pattern for verifying print fixes.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in iter6. Iter6 changes are pure security hardening: (1) printInvoice was previously using window.open + child.document.write(html) which would render an attacker-controlled invoice item name (or customer name with HTML tags) as raw DOM in a new window context; the new path uses srcdoc on a hidden iframe with all dynamic values passed through escapeHtml (& → &, < → <, > → >, " → ", ' → ') — verified by inspecting the srcdoc post-click and confirming no raw <script> sequence outside the inert <style> block. (2) The `inv`/`dt` variable rename in server.py was a dead-code cleanup with no functional change — regression tests confirm endpoints still return identical contracts.
